themes_detail.label: Illegal fireworks surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints spiked to 3 this week, a 1100% jump from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden emergence of dangerous nighttime disturbances in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 3 illegal fireworks complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35)
1100% spike represents acute departure from typical activity
Timeframe: first week of May, potential seasonal pattern pre-summer
reporting_angles: Interview residents in blocks with multiple complaints about safety fears and sleep disruption
Check NYPD enforcement records: are officers responding to 311 calls, and what is arrest/citation rate?

themes_detail.label: Dead and dying trees crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 8 this week from a 1.1 weekly average, a 611% spike (z-score: 5.04), suggesting rapid deterioration of the district's street canopy that could signal disease, neglect, or environmental stress.
evidence: 8 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.04)
Concentrated timeline suggests district-wide pattern rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Map the 8 complaints geographically—are trees dying in specific neighborhoods or along particular corridors?
Contact NYC Parks: what is their assessment of tree health in CD 309, and are they triaging removals/replanting?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints surged to 18 this week from a 5.4 weekly average, a 235% spike (z-score: 4.86), indicating a sudden increase in loud cars, motorcycles, or trucks disrupting residential quality of life.
evidence: 18 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs 5.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.86)
235% increase marks sharp departure from typical pattern
Coincides with warmer weather, potential seasonal surge in motorcycle activity
reporting_angles: Identify hotspots: which streets/avenues are generating the most vehicle noise complaints this week?
Interview residents on those blocks about repeat offenders, times of day, and what enforcement they've seen from NYPD

themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion (earlier spike)
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 97 three weeks ago, a 1840% spike from the 5.0 weekly average (z-score: 12.82), representing the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset, though the spike has already occurred and current status is unclear.
evidence: 97 graffiti complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 5.0 weekly average (z-score: 12.82, highest severity)
1840% spike is the largest percentage increase in the dataset
Status unclear: verify whether complaints have subsided or if issue persists at elevated levels
reporting_angles: Follow-up verification: pull most recent 1-week graffiti data to determine if spike has resolved or stabilized at new elevated level
Visual survey of high-complaint blocks to document extent of graffiti and assess whether city cleanup has occurred

themes_detail.label: Root/sewer/sidewalk deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 5 last week from a 0.2 weekly average, a 1900% increase (z-score: 10.97), indicating sudden emergence of critical infrastructure hazards affecting pedestrian safety and subsurface stability.
evidence: 5 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 10.97)
1900% spike represents acute infrastructure failure signal
Potential safety hazard: roots lifting sidewalks, sewer backups, or sinkhole risk
reporting_angles: Identify the 5 complaint locations and visit to document hazards: are sidewalks cracked/buckled, are sewers backing up, or are tree roots exposed?
Contact DEP: are there known sewer issues or aging infrastructure in these blocks, and what is repair timeline?
